title: Merge Sort
description: Learn how Merge Sort uses Divide and Conquer to sort data efficiently through recursive splitting and merging.

sections.title: Introduction
sections.content:
Simple sorting algorithms become inefficient when working with very large datasets.

Merge Sort improves performance by using the Divide and Conquer paradigm to split large problems into smaller manageable parts.

This strategy allows Merge Sort to maintain efficient performance even as dataset size grows.

sections.title: Dividing the Array
sections.content:
Merge Sort repeatedly divides the array into smaller halves.

The splitting process continues recursively until each subarray contains only one element.

At this point, each individual subarray is already considered sorted.

sections.title: Merging Sorted Subarrays
sections.content:
After dividing the array, Merge Sort begins combining smaller sorted subarrays together.

During the merge phase, elements are compared carefully to ensure the final combined array remains sorted.

This repeated merging process eventually produces one fully sorted collection.

sections.title: Stable Sorting
sections.content:
Merge Sort is considered a stable sorting algorithm.

Stable sorting means elements with equal values maintain their original relative order after sorting.

This property becomes important in systems that process multiple sorting conditions or structured datasets.

sections.title: Organizing Papers Analogy
sections.content:
Imagine sorting a large stack of papers.

Instead of sorting the entire stack at once, you first divide the papers into smaller piles, organize each pile separately, and then combine the sorted piles together.

This mirrors how Merge Sort processes data.

sections.title: Merge Sort in Real Systems
sections.content:
Merge Sort is widely used in large-scale data processing systems because of its predictable efficiency.

It is especially useful for sorting linked structures, external storage data, and distributed datasets where stable sorting behavior is important.

sections.title: Lesson Summary
sections.content: Merge Sort uses Divide and Conquer to sort data efficiently by recursively splitting arrays and merging sorted subarrays together. Its stable behavior and logarithmic efficiency make it suitable for large-scale applications.
